Senses.Explanation: The staff is first a walking stick; in the Chan hall it is also a handled teaching-seat implement. Records make its use visible by narrating named figures raising, planting, pointing, throwing down, or striking with it. The staff-holder performs the act, while the recorder normally supplies the action wording; only a headword actually spoken inside quoted words is assigned to that utterer.

Senses.Note: 14 exact evidence rows from 8 independent works are stored for this sense.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Gateless Checkpoint (無門關), case 44, “Bajiao's Staff” (芭蕉拄杖), explicitly records Bajiao Huiqing addressing the assembly and giving and taking away the staff.
The Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), in Yuanwu Keqin's commentary, quotes Yunmen Wenyan's dragon saying and its explicit return to “just one staff” (只是一條拄杖子) in one contiguous span.
Boshan's Recorded Sayings, complete hall address: after the recorder narrates Boshan planting the staff, Boshan directly says, ‘The staff can discern it.’
Blue Cliff Record, complete Yuanwu commentary: Yuanwu Keqin quotes Yunmen's instruction to call a staff simply a staff. Yuanwu is the utterer of the stored wording; Yunmen is its quoted source.

The Recorded Sayings of Master Fangrong Xi (方融璽禪師語錄), in Fangrong Xi's “Instructions for Travelling on Foot” (行腳垂示), sets calling and not calling the object a staff side by side. Fangrong Xi is not yet on the roster.
Source narration in Source Record (古尊宿語錄) owns the headword-bearing report. Yunmen Wenyan is the participant described.

Occurrences.Kwic: 汾陽示眾曰識得拄杖子行脚事畢
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linked Collection of Chan Lineage Verse Comments on Old Cases (禪宗頌古聯珠通集) explicitly introduces Fenyang Shanzhao's assembly saying: recognizing the staff completes travelling on foot. This occurrence is trimmed to Fenyang's exact speaker-owned turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 三角云識得拄杖子入地獄如箭
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linked Collection of Chan Lineage Verse Comments on Old Cases (禪宗頌古聯珠通集) attributes the opposed saying to Sanjiao. The parallel in Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters names the speaker Letan Huaicheng and gives the fuller form: recognizing the staff sends one to hell like an arrow. This occurrence is trimmed to Letan's exact speaker-owned turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 過去諸佛現在諸佛未來諸佛西天二十八祖唐土六祖天下老和尚緫變成南源拄杖子去也
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), in the record of Ciming Chuyuan, records Ciming making the buddhas of the three times, the Indian and Chinese patriarchs, and all old masters become Nanyuan's staff.

Occurrences.Kwic: 拄杖子是衲僧尋常用底。因什麼却道途路不得力。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄) records Yuanwu Keqin directly calling the staff an ordinary implement of a patched-robed monk and asking why it is ineffective on the road.

Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), in the record of Yunmen Wenyan, records Yunmen locally calling this staff “complete command” (三昧) and tying recognition of it to recognition of the old masters under heaven.

Senses.Explanation: The staff is a teaching and testing implement: named masters identify it, transfer it, raise or break it, and predicate impossible actions of it while disagreeing over whether recognizing it completes travel or leads to hell. The exact rows retain their separate speakers, narrators, participants, and quoted layers; no single deployment is made to resolve all others.
